I'm tentatively teaching a course on Lean and math formalization in Fall 2027. This is a page to dump various resources for future use. I used to do this a lot in the past but things have been changing so fast that it has been hard to keep up.

## Learning Lean

| Resource | What it is |
|---|---|
| [Mathematics in Lean](https://leanprover-community.github.io/mathematics_in_lean/) | A tactic-focused course for mathematicians, with exercises, built on Mathlib. |
| [Theorem Proving in Lean 4](https://lean-lang.org/theorem_proving_in_lean4/) | The official foundations text: dependent type theory, propositions and proofs, inductive types and tactics. |
| [Lean Game Server](https://adam.math.hhu.de/) | Interactive games for learning Lean, including the Natural Number Game. |
| [Lean 4 Web](https://live.lean-lang.org/) | Lean in the browser, with nothing to install. |

## Tools

| Resource | What it is |
|---|---|
| [Loogle](https://loogle.lean-lang.org/) | Search Lean and Mathlib definitions and theorems by type signature or pattern. ([source](https://github.com/nomeata/loogle)) |
| [LeanSearch](https://leansearch.net/), [LeanExplore](https://www.leanexplore.com/) | Search Lean libraries in natural language, which helps when you don't yet know the Lean name. |
| [Verso](https://verso.lean-lang.org/) | A platform for writing documents, books, course materials and websites in Lean. |
| [Paperproof](https://github.com/Paper-Proof/paperproof) | A VS Code extension that shows a Lean proof as a tree, closer to a pen-and-paper proof. Probably most useful for beginners. |
| [leanblueprint](https://github.com/PatrickMassot/leanblueprint) | Plan a formalization as a LaTeX blueprint, with a dependency graph linked to the Lean declarations. The standard way to organize a group project. ([LeanArchitect](https://github.com/hanwenzhu/LeanArchitect) generates blueprint data from the Lean code itself.) |

## AI and Lean

| Resource | What it is |
|---|---|
| [LeanDojo](https://leandojo.org/) | Open-source toolkits, data and benchmarks for machine learning on Lean. ([paper](https://arxiv.org/abs/2306.15626)) |
| [Lean Copilot](https://github.com/lean-dojo/LeanCopilot) | LLM-based proof suggestions and premise search inside Lean. |
| [lean-lsp-mcp](https://github.com/oOo0oOo/lean-lsp-mcp) | A Model Context Protocol server that gives AI coding agents access to Lean's goals, diagnostics and search. |
| [REPL](https://github.com/leanprover-community/repl), [Pantograph](https://github.com/leanprover/Pantograph) | Machine-to-machine interfaces to Lean, which AI tools build on to run proofs and inspect a project. |
| [lean4-skills](https://github.com/cameronfreer/lean4-skills) | Claude Code skills for AI-assisted formalization of your own project, with a draft, prove, review, refactor workflow and autonomy levels from interactive to fully autonomous. |
| [Tau Ceti](https://lean-lang.org/use-cases/tau-ceti) | A Lean library downstream of Mathlib, written and reviewed largely by AI, with humans setting roadmaps and review rubrics. ([repository](https://reservoir.lean-lang.org/@TauCetiProject/TauCeti)) |
| [Aristotle](https://aristotle.harmonic.fun/) | Harmonic's Lean prover, which can be called from an agent to fill in lemmas. Access is limited. |
| [Kimina-Prover](https://huggingface.co/blog/AI-MO/kimina-prover) | A Lean 4 theorem-proving model from Project Numina and Moonshot AI, trained with reinforcement learning. |
| [DeepSeek-Prover-V2](https://huggingface.co/deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-Prover-V2-7B) | Open-weight Lean 4 provers (7B and 671B) that break a problem into subgoals and prove each one. |

## Projects and examples

| Resource | What it is |
|---|---|
| [Lean community projects](https://leanprover-community.github.io/lean_projects.html) | A list of ongoing formalization projects. |
| [Formal Conjectures](https://github.com/google-deepmind/formal-conjectures) | Google DeepMind's collection of formalized statements of open conjectures, a source of ambitious project ideas. |
| [The Equational Theories Project](https://arxiv.org/abs/2512.07087) | A large collaborative project led by Terence Tao that settled over 22 million implications between equational laws of magmas, all formalized in Lean. |
| [The Stacks Project](https://axiommath.ai/research/the-stacks-project-formalized/) | The Stacks Project, formalized in Lean by AxiomMath. |
| [Rubik's cube in Lean](https://github.com/vihdzp/rubik-lean4) | A proof that there are $2^{12} \times 3^{8} \times 8! \times 11!$ Rubik's cube positions, verified in Lean. |
